issue.title: e2e: a needle names a key, it never spells one (review needed)

repository.name: CodeAF
repository.description: Open-Source Software factory for Open Models

issue.body:
Closes #998.

## What was wrong

`TestQuestionsE2E` has been **14 of 18 red since #933** (`23f5da1eb`), which took
the brackets off every key on this surface. The line draws `▸1 delete it`; the
suite waited three minutes at a time for `[1] delete it`.

The untagged gate that exists precisely so this cannot happen (#184) stayed green
throughout, because it was looking at the half of each needle that had not moved:

- nine needles in `internal/e2e/questions_e2e_test.go` were **inline literals**,
  which the table's gate cannot see at all — it only reads `tuiwords_test.go`; and
- **eleven rows of the table itself** spelled `[c] change` in `screen` while their
  `source` said only `change`. The gate greps `source` against the surface's own
  sources, so it checked the word and never the key in front of it.

The second half is the larger share and is not in the issue's own list:
`questionLaterKeyWord`, `questionTakeThePickWord`, `questionChangeKeyWord`,
`questionUndoKeyWord`, `questionTickKeyWord`, `questionBlankKeyWord`,
`questionPairAWord`, `questionPairBWord`, `questionMoveItWord` — plus the four
landing answers used by `TestTUIE2E` and `TestTaskStatesE2E` (`settleAccept`,
`settleNotRight`, `settleTellIt`, `settleConflictNo`), rotted the same way.

The paid run then found two more of the same shape, one layer down:

- **the chip.** `questionChipTail` waited for `question · alt+a`. The status line
  leads with the question's own head — `? delete the build directory? · alt+a` —
  and spells `1 question` only where there is no head. Its `source` was `alt+a`,
  so the gate was green on it exactly as on the brackets. The row is its own name
  now: the tail, ` · alt+a`.
- **the aiming rule.** `o`, `c`, `x`, `?` are each the first letter of a word
  people type into the box, so the block does not take one from somebody who has
  not yet aimed at the question (`questionAimKey`; the manual says it in a
  person's words). Six scenarios pressed `o` to open a page, the `o` went into the
  message box, and each waited out its patience for a page nobody opened — with
  `› o` on the screen it printed.
- **the room's foot.** It waited for `nothing chosen yet` on a freshly opened
  page. Since #789 the page opens where the block's pointer stood, so it says
  `answering 1 postgres`.

## The fix — one abstraction

A row that is offered on a key now **names the key**, and one function puts the
two together:

- `tuiWord` gains `key`; `say` returns `tuiWord.spelling()` — the word alone on a
  plain row, `keyedWord(key, word)` on a keyed one.
- **`keyedWord` is the one place this suite writes the gap between a key and its
  word.** The nine pasted answers go through it, so `delete it` stays the
  scenario's own word (the model was steered to offer it) and the `1 ` in front of
  it stays the product's grammar.
- Nineteen rows are respelled onto it. The one-space column is pinned by
  `internal/tui3`'s own tests, not read off a screenshot — `relanding_test.go`
  asserts `a resolve it   n drop it   s tell it`, `papercuts_test.go` asserts
  `a accept` / `n not right`.
- `aim` is the gesture, spelled once: `↓` then `↑`, because an aim may not be an
  answer — `enter` takes the pick and `esc` puts the question away — so the walk
  is walked straight back and the pointer ends where it started.

## The law that keeps it

`TestNoNeedleSpellsAKeyTheSurfaceStoppedSpelling` (untagged, `go/ast`, 0.02 s)
walks every screen-reading call in the package — `awaitQuestion`, `screenSays`,
`screenSilent`, `screenEchoes`, `r.waitFor`, `statesAwait` — and refuses a
**needle-position** literal that brackets a key or pastes a numbered answer onto
its word. It reads the table as data (so a bracketed `screen` is caught too) and
the suite as source.

Needle positions are named per door rather than "every literal in the call",
because the last argument of the three assertions is a *moment* — prose for
whoever reads the failure. Every other literal is left alone on purpose: the
suite's own header says a sentence the **model** wrote is a coincidence, not a
source of truth.

Both halves were proved to fire, on the Spark, against this branch:

```
--- FAIL: TestNoNeedleSpellsAKeyTheSurfaceStoppedSpelling (0.02s)
    tuiwords_test.go:1171: questions_e2e_test.go:334: screenSays waits for "[2] leave it", and this
      surface stopped bracketing its keys in #933. Say it with keyedWord(<key>, <word>), or with
      say(t, …) where the word is the product's.

--- FAIL: TestNoNeedleSpellsAKeyTheSurfaceStoppedSpelling (0.02s)
    tuiwords_test.go:1175: questions_e2e_test.go:984: awaitQuestion waits for "1 overwrite it",
      which pastes an answer's key onto its word. The key grammar is the product's and moves
      without this file: say it with keyedWord("1", "overwrite it").
```

Manual: `internal/manual/chat/questions.md` said a key is drawn `[1] allow once`.
It is drawn `1 allow once`.

## Evidence (Spark, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`)

Untagged gate, on the merge candidate — green in a third of a second:

```
ok  	github.com/Agent-Field/aforge-v2/internal/e2e	0.353s
```

`internal/manual` green (`ok … 1.723s`). `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` clean;
`make changelog-check` clean.

`go test -tags e2e -run TestQuestionsE2E -count=1 -timeout 60m -v ./internal/e2e/`,
three paid runs, tmux `af-e2eneedles`. **4/18 on `dev` → 16/18**, and the
timeouts are gone (`ALineAsks…` 212 s → 13 s, `AQuestionWhoseSubjectWentAway…`
187 s → 10 s, `AnotherWindowAnswers…` 200 s → 22 s):

```
--- FAIL: TestQuestionsE2E (522.58s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ALineAsksAndTheKeysAnswerIt (13.37s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ACardCountsDownToItsPickAndEnterTakesIt (9.13s)
    --- FAIL: TestQuestionsE2E/TheRoomComparesAnnotatesAsksBackAndSends (265.03s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ACardWithABlockUnderEachAnswerArrivesWhole (29.67s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ASentenceWithHolesIsFilledIn (17.52s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/AChecklistTicksSeveralAnswers (17.75s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/PairsAreAnsweredOneRowAtATime (13.99s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ADialIsMovedWithTheArrows (14.76s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/ARatifiedActSaysWhatItDidAndHowToUndoIt (5.81s)
    --- FAIL: TestQuestionsE2E/AssumptionsStandUntilOneIsStruck (8.65s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/TwoQuestionsInOneStepAreOnePanelWithTabs (20.74s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/FourReadsInOneBatchAreOnePermissionFrame (17.74s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/AnotherWindowAnswersAndTheFirstSaysWho (21.93s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/AQuestionWhoseSubjectWentAwayIsWithdrawn (10.70s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/AProjectRuleDecidesAChoiceAndTheRowWearsIt (15.75s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/HeadlessTakesTheDefaultAndSaysSo (18.18s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/TheOrdinaryRoadCarriesAQuestionAndItsAnswer (17.67s)
    --- PASS: TestQuestionsE2E/TheOlderBlocksHaveNotMovedOntoTheObject (4.19s)
```

## It is not 18/18, and the three reds are product defects, filed

Not needles. Each one is something the suite could not reach while it was waiting
for screens that no longer existed, and each is reproducible:

- **#1005** — a question whose answers do not fit the row is drawn as a row
  anyway, with an answer cut off. `questionRowFits` exists, its own doc says the
  chooser asks it, and `grep -rn questionRowFits internal/tui3/` finds no caller:
  the ladder's last rung is `return true`. Fires 3 of 3 runs
  (`AssumptionsStandUntilOneIsStruck`). Fixing it changes which drawing questions
  get across the product, so it wants the owner's eye and a full `internal/tui3`
  run — not this PR.
- **#1006** — an ask-back on a turn-blocking question lets the turn end, and the
  question is withdrawn out from under the person: `⊘ … — no longer needed · the
  turn moved on without it`, with their answer half-composed. Fires 2 of 2 runs
  that reached it (`TheRoomComparesAnnotatesAsksBackAndSends`).
- **#1007** — `ask`'s `options` sent as a JSON string carrying `blocks` is still
  refused (`options takes a list; it arrived as text`); `unwrapEncoded` does not
  fire on the nested shape. Model-dependent, ~2 runs in 3
  (`ACardWithABlockUnderEachAnswerArrivesWhole`, green in the run above).

So #998's acceptance is met in substance — the suite waits for the screens the
surface draws, and a law stops it drifting again — and the remaining red is real
findings rather than rot.
